headline_marked: [[Man found dead]] with mouth taped on Dhaka Elevated Expressway
headline: Man found dead with mouth taped on Dhaka Elevated Expressway
summary: Police suspect the victim, believed to be around 50, was murdered elsewhere and dumped on the expressway in Banani.
details: Police recovered the body of an unidentified man from the Dhaka Elevated Expressway in Banani yesterday morning.
The victim, estimated to be around 50 years old, was found with his mouth taped, suggesting a violent crime.
He was wearing a blue outfit similar to those commonly worn by CNG-run auto-rickshaw drivers.
Banani Police Station Officer-in-Charge Faridul Islam stated that they suspect the victim was murdered elsewhere and the body was dumped on the expressway during the night or early morning.
Police are currently reviewing CCTV footage from cameras installed along the expressway to identify those involved and determine how the body was placed there.
Efforts are ongoing to establish the identity of the deceased man.

headline_marked: 1,938 iPhones seized: [[6 Chinese nationals arrested]] in Cox's Bazar
headline: 1,938 iPhones seized: 6 Chinese nationals arrested in Cox's Bazar
summary: Police raided a hotel on the Marine Drive road, uncovering a massive haul of electronics and communication gear used for online scams.
details: Police arrested six Chinese nationals from Hotel Sea Palace in Cox's Bazar following a raid conducted between Thursday night and Friday morning.
The operation resulted in the seizure of 1,938 iPhones, 40 laptops, and various communication tools, including equipment reportedly used by foreign police.
The arrests were based on information provided by Dhaka police and a complaint filed at the Ramu police station regarding online-based fraud.
According to Ramu Police Station OC AK Fazlul Haque, the suspects were arrested under the Cyber Security Act for their alleged involvement in online scams.
Local residents and police reported that some Chinese and Taiwanese nationals had been renting two hotels along the Marine Drive road for at least two months.
The suspects were produced before the Cox's Bazar Amli Court on Friday afternoon, where the court ordered them to be sent to jail.
Police officials stated that raids are continuing to bring other individuals involved in this fraudulent network to justice.
caption:
Nearly 2,000 iPhones and 40 laptops seized in a single hotel raid. Six Chinese nationals are now in custody for running online scams.

Police arrested six Chinese nationals from Hotel Sea Palace in Cox's Bazar following a raid conducted between Thursday night and Friday morning.

The operation resulted in the seizure of 1,938 iPhones, 40 laptops, and various communication tools, including equipment reportedly used by foreign police.

The arrests were based on information provided by Dhaka police and a complaint filed at the Ramu police station regarding online-based fraud.

According to Ramu Police Station OC AK Fazlul Haque, the suspects were arrested under the Cyber Security Act for their alleged involvement in online scams.

Local residents and police reported that some Chinese and Taiwanese nationals had been renting two hotels along the Marine Drive road for at least two months.

The suspects were produced before the Cox's Bazar Amli Court on Friday afternoon, where the court ordered them to be sent to jail.

Police officials stated that raids are continuing to bring other individuals involved in this fraudulent network to justice.
